L33: Anthropogenic sources, especially industrial, emit into the atmosphere gases and aerosols, which play an important role in atmospheric exchanges. The use of new hyperspectral airborne sensors in the infrared range at high spatial resolution opens the way for further improvements in the characterization of industrial plumes.
L34: Existing methods, based on linear or Bayesian approach, present two major limitations: the heterogeneous environment impact on retrievals and the spatial and vertical extents of the plume are not considered. In this paper, a new method for plume characterization is presented to overcome such limitations. This method uses an accurate non linear formalism of cloud gas radiative impact.
L35: It includes furthermore a ground classification of the scene, in order to take into account the soil heterogeneity and spectral behaviour. This strategy will be validated using synthetic scenes of industrial area, and real data from Telops Hyper-Cam airborne platform.

L93: ABSTRACT
L94: 
L95: Anthropogenic sources, especially industrial, emit into the at-
L96: 
L97: mosphere gases and aerosols, which play an important role
L98: 
L99: in atmospheric exchanges. The use of new hyperspectral air-
L100: 
L101: borne sensors in the infrared range at high spatial resolution
L102: opens the way for further improvements in the characteriza-
L103: 
L104: tion of industrial plumes. Existing methods, based on linear
L105: 
L106: or Bayesian approach, present two major limitations: the het-
L107: 
L108: erogeneous environment impact on retrievals and the spatial
L109: 
L110: and vertical extents of the plume are not considered.
L111: 
L112: In this paper, a new method for plume characterization is pre-
L113: 
L114: sented to overcome such limitations. This method uses an
L115: 
L116: accurate non linear formalism of cloud gas radiative impact.
L117: It includes furthermore a ground classiﬁcation of the scene,
L118: 
L119: in order to take into account the soil heterogeneity and spec-
L120: 
L121: tral behaviour. This strategy will be validated using synthetic
L122: 
L123: scenes of industrial area, and real data from Telops Hyper-
L124: 
L125: Cam airborne platform.

L131: 1. INTRODUCTION
L132: 
L133: Anthropogenic sources, especially industrial, are involved
L134: with a major contribution to air pollution. However, these
L135: 
L136: emissions remain poorly estimated at a high spatial resolu-
L137: 
L138: tion. Recent technological advances in terms of spatial and
L139: 
L140: spectral resolutions of thermal infrared airborne hyperspectral
L141: 
L142: sensors, open a way of improving gaseous efﬂuents charac-
L143: 
L144: terization, since the majority of gas have their signatures in
L145: 
L146: the thermal domain.
L147: 
L148: In literature different approaches were proposed to quan-
L149: 
L150: tify gaseous efﬂuents using hyperspectral infrared imagery.
L151: Assuming plume gases are optically thin, Young [1] intro-
L152: 
L153: duces a linear formalism to retrieve plume integrated column
L154: 
L155: concentration of each pixel. A linear least-squares regression
L156: 
L157: method is used to determine the thermal contrast, which is di-
L158: 
L159: rectly related to the integrated column concentration.
L160: 
L161: Heasler, et al. [2] follow a Bayesian approach. They devel-
L162: 
L163: oped a non-linear regression using the Metropolis-Hastings
L164: 
L165: algorithm. The atmospheric terms are supposed to be known.
L166: As the background clutter (ground temperature and emissiv-
L167: 
L168: ity) is the dominant source of variability, it is handled as nui-
L169: 
L170: sance parameters.
L171: 
L172: A previous study [3] showed some of the limitations of
L173: 
L174: such characterization methods. First, the spatial and vertical
L175: 
L176: extents of the plume are not taken into account in these meth-
L177: 
L178: ods, which induces a miscalculation of the plume radiative
L179: 
L180: impact. Then, the heterogeneous environment of an indus-
L181: trial scene impact a lot on the retrieval performances of these
L182: 
L183: methods [4].
L184: 
L185: Hereinafter, we present a new method of plume characteriza-
L186: 
L187: tion, which takes into account the vertical extent of the plume.
L188: 
L189: Moreover, our retrieval is preceded by a classiﬁcation of the
L190: 
L191: background, in order to deal with soil heterogeneity.
L192: 
L193: The paper is organized in the following way: section 2 is ded-
L194: 
L195: icated to the description of the plume retrieval methodology.
L196: Then, sections 3 and 4 evaluate the application of our method
L197: 
L198: on synthetic data and Telops Hyper-Cam airborne platform
L199: 
L200: data.

L205:

L207: 
L208: scene. To model the radiance at airborne sensor level, the fol-
L209: 
L210: lowing assumptions are done: 1) for each pixel, the ground
L211: 
L212: is assumed to be homogeneous, ﬂat and lambertian. 2) The
L213: 
L214: plume is modeled as a set of ﬂat layers, which are homo-

L225: in our case as we only take into account gas species. Under
